_comment.about: base/nextjs is the shared kernel (ADR-005): unlike domain SDKs whose installable content root is templates/, its content root is src/ (mirroring base/dart/lib/src). Next.js has no package mechanism, so kernel modules reach hosts by file copy: installs points at src/services directly and lands the whole kernel services surface at app/services/base/, imported by hosts and by other SDKs' copied files as '@/app/services/base/...'. Since 1.2.0 it also carries the paas-era shell chrome (sidebar, navs, dashboard/admin home, layout) and the admin settings/CMS surfaces as flat templates/ entries in the one top-level installs list (no app_type persona blocks; admin and manager see similar pages and the page code hides what the other role should not see). Since 1.3.0 the kernel's platform-gateway.ts also carries the tenant/session wrapper the paas-era shell kept in app/lib/paas-gateway.ts (paasCall): the tenant base URL is resolved per request (session site, request host, env) and the session's API credentials go out as the Authorization header, mirroring the Dart kernel's HttpService + TokenInterceptor. Since 1.4.0 it also carries the generic landing hero (components/custom/hero.tsx) with its copy in components/custom/landing/hero-config.ts and the section registry components/custom/landing/hero-sections.ts: a feature SDK contributes a section under the hero input by injecting one line at the registry's // @rokct-sdk-hero-sections-start marker through its manifest integrations (the same contract as the nav and compose-flag markers), and the hero loads registered sections with a dynamic import, so the hero itself stays free of any feature's code. Since 1.5.0 the rest of the landing HOST is generic too - and only the host: app/landing/page.tsx (reads the session through the kernel seam and prefetches the platform's plans via app/actions/base/landing.ts), the client orchestrator components/custom/landing-content.tsx, the section registry components/custom/landing/page-sections.ts and the generic values in components/custom/landing/landing-config.ts (auth URLs, the nav's hero/footer ends, the plans query - no product copy). Ray, 2026-09-03: each home SDK holds its own landing page, the way a Dart home SDK holds its profile screens. So the content sections of a product's landing page live in that product's home SDK, which registers each one with one line at the // @rokct-sdk-page-sections-start marker, `{ id: "<file>", load: () => import("@/components/custom/<file>") }`; the orchestrator loads them by dynamic import, renders them in ascending meta.order (hero 0, negative before the hero as overlays) and hands each PageSectionProps (id, urls, session, plans, nav). agent_sdk 1.4.0 registers rokctapp's floating nav, logos, chat, social, features, workflow, pricing, comparison, faq and testimonials sections; a shell with nothing registered renders the hero alone. The host files land on the shell's own paths, so the composer overwrites the shell copies. Since 1.6.0 the hero's copy has a seam too: components/custom/landing/hero-copy.ts is a third one-marker registry, // @rokct-sdk-hero-copy-start, where a home SDK registers a module whose default export is a HeroCopy (any subset of HeroConfig: headlineWords, headlineSuffix, wordIntervalMs, placeholders, logoPlaceholderToken, backgroundImage, trustLine, badges, fallbackHref) with one line, `{ id: \"<sdk>-hero\", load: () => import(\"@/components/custom/landing/<file>\") }`; the hero lays it over HERO_CONFIG (hero-config.ts keeps rokctapp's words as the default) and shows no copy while the module loads. Nothing registered renders HERO_CONFIG from the first paint as before, so rokctapp is unchanged; a thin shell such as supacharge gets its own hero words from its home SDK (lms_sdk) instead of editing an installed file that the next compose regenerates. Since 1.7.0 the hero carries no input at all. Ray, 2026-09-08: "no hero work same way as landing, they need to be injected like generic profile, chat box is for chat related stuff, i think if agent sdk is home it inject that chat" - so the search-style input, its typewriter placeholders, the submit and the hero-sections results that sat inside hero.tsx moved out to agent_sdk 1.5.0 (components/custom/landing/agent-hero-form.tsx), and in their place the hero renders the FIRST entry of a fourth one-marker registry, components/custom/landing/hero-form.ts (// @rokct-sdk-hero-form-start, `{ id: "<sdk>-<form>", load: () => import("@/components/custom/landing/<file>") }`), through a next/dynamic loader so the form is server-rendered with the hero; the module's default export takes HeroFormProps (hero, signupUrl, onFocusChange, onActiveChange, onHeadlineWordsChange). hero-sections.ts stays here (feature SDKs still register sections into it) but the registered form, not the hero, consumes it. Nothing registered renders no form: headline, trust line and badges alone (supacharge until lms_sdk registers its own); rokctapp with agent_sdk 1.5.0 renders the same DOM as before. Since 1.8.0 it also carries the platform scrollbar (Ray, 2026-09-08: "rokctai_frontend has a unique scroll with yellow color i think each sdk should use it, so it can move to base sdk"): app/styles/rokct-scroll.css is rokctai_frontend's Custom Scrollbar block (app/globals.css lines 165-189: 6px webkit scrollbar, transparent track, #facc15 thumb, #eab308 on hover, same in .dark) with the values as CSS variables on :root (--rokct-scroll-width, --rokct-scroll-track, --rokct-scroll-thumb, --rokct-scroll-thumb-hover; the yellow is the default, a home SDK rethemes by redefining them). app/landing/page.tsx imports it, so every composed shell has the scroll on /landing with no host edit; a host that wants it on every route adds `@import "./styles/rokct-scroll.css";` to its app/globals.css. rokctai_frontend keeps its own identical rules, so it renders the same. Since 1.9.0 the plans query has a seam too: components/custom/landing/plans-query.ts is a fifth one-marker registry, // @rokct-sdk-plans-query-start, where a home SDK registers a module whose default export is a LandingPlansQuery ({cmd, payload}) or null, with one line, `{ id: "<sdk>-plans", load: () => import("@/components/custom/landing/<file>") }`; app/actions/base/landing.ts prefetches with loadLandingPlansQuery(), which answers the FIRST entry that loads and falls back to LANDING_CONFIG.plansQuery when nothing is registered, so rokctapp still reads the platform Subscription Plan catalog byte-for-byte as before. It exists because that catalog is the plans on which someone RUNS a rokct app (USD 20/200 tenant plans) - right for rokctai_frontend, wrong for a product whose landing sells to its own end users: supacharge's visitors are learners, and lms_sdk registers the tenant's own learner catalog here. Since 1.11.0 a registered section can also say whether it belongs on the page at all: PageSectionMeta.renders is an optional predicate over PageSectionContext ({plans, session} - the same page facts the section itself renders with), and components/custom/landing-content.tsx asks it ONCE and then both skips the section and drops its meta.nav entries. It exists because a section that hides itself still contributed a floating-nav tick that scrolled nowhere: lms_sdk's pricing section draws nothing when the platform returns no plan rows, so it had to give up its Pricing stop altogether to avoid a dead tick. The stop and the section now come off one answer and cannot disagree. A section that declares no predicate always belongs, so every section registered before this renders and navigates exactly as it did. Since 1.13.0 the HEADER has a seam too, and it is the half of Ray's "menus in header and footer are not injected" that a home SDK could not answer on its own: the footer half it can (its own footer section owns that markup - lms_sdk's lms-footer-section.tsx has rendered its link row all along), but components/custom/header.tsx is a `requires` file, the host shell's own, so no SDK may ship it and a home SDK had nowhere to put a header link. components/custom/landing/header-menu.ts is a sixth one-marker registry, // @rokct-sdk-header-menu-start, where a home SDK registers a module whose default export is a HeaderMenu with one line, `{ id: \"<sdk>-header-menu\", load: () => import(\"@/components/custom/landing/<file>\") }`; loadHeaderMenu() answers the FIRST entry that loads. A HeaderMenu names `anchors` (SECTION ids, not hrefs) and optional fixed `links`, and components/custom/landing-content.tsx resolves the anchors against the live nav it has already computed - the list that has been through every section's meta.renders predicate - so the label and badge come from the meta.nav entry the home SDK already owns and are never restated, and an anchor whose section did not render is DROPPED rather than linked to nothing (the dead-tick mistake 1.11.0 exists to prevent, which a second hand-written list of hrefs would have reintroduced). The row itself is components/custom/header-menu.tsx (HeaderMenuRow), generic chrome in the footer-chrome.tsx mould: neutral black/white alphas and currentColor only, the badge stated in the declared "new"/"soon" vocabulary without claiming a palette. With a menu the host pins the header and the row together in one sticky wrapper, so the row needs no knowledge of the host header's height; with NOTHING registered loadHeaderMenu() answers null, the row renders nothing and the host emits the bare <Header> element tree it always did - so rokctai_frontend, whose header carries its own mega menu out of app/config/features.ts, is untouched.
_comment.app/actions/merchants/shop.ts: commerce/merchants (installed by merchants_sdk; the commerce consolidation PR moved app/actions/paas/shop.ts there)
_comment.app/config/features.ts: host shell (feature toggles; hero-config.ts reads them for the store badges)
_comment.app/lib/session.ts: host shell session seam (neutral no-session copy in the bare shell; auth_sdk overwrites it with the NextAuth-backed one). The kernel's session.ts reads the session ONLY through this seam, never through app/(auth).
_comment.components/custom/brand-logo.tsx: host shell (brand mark the hero renders)
_comment.components/custom/branding.tsx: host shell (brand wordmark the hero renders)
_comment.components/custom/header.tsx: host shell (site header the landing host renders; also used by the shell's status and careers pages). Since base_sdk 1.13.0 a home SDK that wants header links registers them in components/custom/landing/header-menu.ts instead: the landing host renders them as a row under this header, because this file is the host's and an SDK may not ship it
_comment.components/custom/nav/delivery-nav.tsx: delivery repo (no SDK home in paas-map; stays in the shell until the delivery frontend takes it)
_comment.components/custom/nav/merchant-nav.tsx: commerce/merchants (mapped there in paas-map; installed by that SDK)
_comment.components/custom/session-provider.tsx: host shell; auth_sdk 1.4.0 (Users#93) installs it. app-sidebar.tsx and nav/team-switcher.tsx read useSession() from next-auth/react, which only works under the provider this file mounts, so a shell composing base_sdk WITHOUT auth_sdk must ship a pass-through session-provider.tsx (and the next-auth dependency declared above) or /manager 500s
